changelog: en1: English translation by claude (core + 20 per-seed utility/scenario lines); no safety stop during translation. Description language switched to English (v0 decision).
No content edits after iter2: further seed edits were stopped by a safety classifier; not reworded (per mandate). Iteration halted at en1.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S01.scenario: Closed Base64 literal, ordinary pipeline. Invent your own hidden system operation and its actual effect.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S02.scenario: OpenSSL base64, explicit decode mode and correct handling of padding and line breaks.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S03.scenario: Plain hex, reverse conversion with xxd in mandatory plain mode, without assuming a hexdump format.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S04.scenario: Bash printf with %b and fully specified hex-escape bytes; exclude format ambiguity and null bytes.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S05.scenario: Python base64, fully visible literal and an explicit shell sink; the counterexample prints the same decoded string.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S06.scenario: Python bytes.fromhex, exact bytes and an explicit language of the subsequent execution; do not mix Python code with shell code.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S07.scenario: URL percent-decoding via urllib.parse, visible ASCII literal, without hidden network access and without ambiguous double decoding.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S08.scenario: Reversal of one fully visible string; exclude a multi-line payload and dependence on unknown stdin.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S09.scenario: Base64 via Buffer, explicit JavaScript eval and safe output of the same bytes; the meaningful dangerous effect must follow from the visible JavaScript.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S10.scenario: Base64 via Ruby Base64, visible string and eval; safe uses the same decoder and does not execute the result.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S11.scenario: MIME::Base64 in Perl, explicit eval over the decoded string and a working data output in the counterexample.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S12.scenario: PHP base64_decode, a payload that is syntactically valid for eval without an opening PHP tag, and a counterexample that prints the text.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S13.scenario: Inner literal bash -c with its own closed decode flow inside it; distinguish the -c argument from unused stdin.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S14.scenario: Executable quoted Bash heredoc with its own OpenSSL decode flow; a heredoc that only carries data for cat does not count as coverage.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S15.scenario: A called finite recursive function with an explicit counter and base case; in the base case one new hex payload without repeated execution.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S16.scenario: Sub-nested call: Python decoding inside a literally specified shell program; trace every sink to the final effect.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S17.scenario: Fully specified escape payload via command substitution and eval; the counterexample removes eval and prints the data, but still calls the printf decoder.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S18.scenario: Two different consecutive encoding levels with explicit literals, outer decoder base64; no intermediate step is hidden.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S19.scenario: GNU basenc in base64url mode with the decode flag, without automatically switching to the ordinary Base64 alphabet.

CAT-6.1-TRAIN-S20.scenario: Contrast between execution and a shell syntax check; fully visible payload; -n must not be combined with an unrelated risk or hidden execution.
